criteria.reason: The shared identifier validator and rooted storage layer reject hostile traversal, separators, absolute and volume paths, controls, non-ASCII input, and noncanonical encodings before identifier-controlled access; focused hostile and full-suite receipts pass.

Runtime isolation records whether state was automatically created, removes owned state through deferred cleanup on success and terminal errors, and preserves caller-owned roots; focused failure-path tests and the full suite pass.

The root installs an exhaustive runnable-operation inventory and enforces structured output and dry-run policy before handlers; inventory, hidden-command fail-closed, flag-shadow, rejection, and mutation-snapshot tests pass.

Advertised JSON spellings are negotiated through the shared contract and tested for parseability and semantic equivalence across prefix, suffix, and collision placements; generated command-reference parity passes and the stale eval help reference is absent.

Streaming output is bounded and reports byte, truncation, and exit facts, but subprocess.Result has no cleanup field or status. Results therefore do not disclose the relevant cleanup facts required by GO-5.

Caller cancellation, deadlines, bounded waits, and POSIX descendant termination are implemented and tested, but Run returns context or wait errors before examining cleanupErr. Cleanup failure is suppressed on cancellation and abnormal-exit paths, so the required cleanup outcome is not reported.

Canonical typed receipts bound to the exact final manifest report exit zero with matching command-output hashes for focused tests, full tests, race, vet, pinned lint, regeneration parity, and Windows amd64 cross-compilation.

The author-distinct validator checked the exact detached commit, frozen intent, manifests, complete 74-path effect, active epoch-1 proof identity, and criterion-level typed evidence; the Windows behavioral limitation is recorded explicitly.

findings.summary: subprocess.Result contains only stdout, stderr, combined output, and exit code, while Run discards cleanupErr whenever context cancellation or wait failure is returned first. Cleanup outcomes remain undisclosed on terminal paths required by GO-5 and GO-6.

not_checked: Windows process-tree cleanup behavior was not executed on this macOS host; no behavioral claim is made beyond source inspection and amd64 cross-compilation.
